sections.description:
Short title extent and commencement

ACT IX OF 1999
NORTH-WEST
FRONTIER PROVINCE TRANSFUSION OF SAFE BLOOD ACT, 1999
ACT IX OF 1999
An Act to regulate
transfusion of safe blood and its products
[Gazette of
N.-W.F.P., Extraordinary, 13th October, 1999]
No.PA/NWFP/Legis.I/99/24250,
dated 13-10-1999.--The North- West Frontier- Province Transfusion of Safe Blood
Bill, 1999 having been passed by the Provincial Assembly of North-West Frontier
Province on the 22nd September, 1999 and assented to by the Governor of the
North-West Frontier Province on 7th October, 1999, is hereby published as an
Act of the Provincial Legislature of North-West Frontier Province.
1. Short title, extent and
commencement. ---(I) This Act may be called the North-West Frontier
Province Transfusion of Safe Blood Act, 1999.
(2) It shall extend to whole of
the North-West Frontier Province.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

2. Definitions. ---In this
Act unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context--
(a) "Authority" means
the Provincial Blood Transfusion. Authority, established under section 5 of
this Act;
(b) "Blood Bank"
includes all organizations carrying out all or any of the purposes of
receiving, preserving, storing, analyzing, screening, processing and issuing of
blood or blood products, whether maintained by Government or by public or
private sector.
(c) "Council" means the
Pakistan Medical and Dental Council established under the Pakistan Medical and
Dental Council Ordinance, 1962 (XXXII of 1962);
(d) "Government" means
the Government of the North West Frontier Province;
(e) "Prescribed" means
prescribed by rules made under this Act.
(f) "Safe blood" means
human blood which is healthy and free from human immunodeficiency (HIV)
Hepatitis B and C viruses, and infective agents like Malarial Parasite and
treponema Palidum and other infective agents, screening of which may be found
essential in future; and
(g) "Schedule" means
the schedule appended to this Act.

3. Transfusion of safe blood.--Every
physical, surgeon and other medical practitioner registered as such under the
Pakistan Medical and Dental Council Ordinance, 1962 (XXXII of 1962), while
transfusing blood to a patient, shall ensure that the blood being transfused is
duly certified as safe - blood by a registered Blood Bank after carrying out
due tests necessary for issuing the requisite certificate.

dated 13-10-1999.--The North- West Frontier- Province Transfusion of Safe Blood
Bill, 1999 having been passed by the Provincial Assembly of North-West Frontier
Province on the 22nd September, 1999 and assented to by the Governor of the
North-West Frontier Province on 7th October, 1999, is hereby published as an
Act of the Provincial Legislature of North-West Frontier Province.
6. Functions of the Authority.-The
functions of the Authority shall be to--
(a) adopt a uniform policy
regarding all aspects of safe blood transfusion based on the current state of
science acid technology issued by National Blood Transfusion Authority, if any,
established by law by the Federal Government;
(b) register and issue licences
to blood banks in the prescribed manner;
(c) renew licences issued to
blood banks annually on payment of such fees as may be prescribed, subject to
the condition that the instructions issued by it for safe blood transfusion
were being followed by the Blood Bank;
(d) prescribed registration and
licence fees debitable to the relevant head of accounts;
(e) fix service charges of blood
and blood products;
(f) ensure that bio-safety
measures specified in the Schedule and instructions issued by the World Health
Organisation (WHO) are strictly adhered to by the Blood Bank.
(g) ensure that the blood banks
are managed and run by qualified professionals having qualifications in blood
transfusion, preferably Haematology and alternately clinical pathology
recognised by the Council; and
(h) monitor the working of the
blood by periodical inspections.

Functions and responsibilities of Blood Banks

dated 13-10-1999.--The North- West Frontier- Province Transfusion of Safe Blood
Bill, 1999 having been passed by the Provincial Assembly of North-West Frontier

North-West Frontier Province on 7th October, 1999, is hereby published as an
Act of the Provincial Legislature of North-West Frontier Province.
7. Functions and
responsibilities of Blood Banks.--Every blood bank shall--
(a) maintain a separate
department, equipment and staff for the purpose of receiving blood donations
and for section, handling, care and safety of the donors;
(b) select donors of blood in
accordance with the instructions issued by the Authority;
(c) cause the donated blood and
blood products to be screened, to ensure that the blood is a safe blood and
record a certificate to this effect on each blood bag meant for transfusion;
(d) possess equipment required
for haemoglobin estimation, blood grouping, cross matching, antibodies
detection and screening of infectious agents including human immunodeficiency,
Hepatitis B and C viruses, Malaria, Syphilis and any other communicable disease
as may be determined by the Authority;
(e) equip itself with proper
reservation and storage of blood products and ensure un-interrupted power supply
for refrigeration;
(f) observe standard operation
procedure approved by the Authority and more particularly specified in the
bye-laws as may be framed by the Authority;
(g) not accept blood from
professional blood donors; and
(h) submit periodical reports to
the Authority in respect of blood donations received by it with break-up of
blood groups, detection of anti bodies and screening of infectious agents.

shall be punishable with imprisonment for a period not less than six months,
which may extend to three years or with fine which shall not be less than fifty
thousand rupees and may extend to one hundred thousand rupees, or with both.

contravention.--No Court shall take cognizance of any contravention under
this Act, except on a complaint in writing made by the Chairman of the
Authority or a person authorised by him; provided that this will not debar the
person aggrieved by any such contravention to seek remedy of his grievance
through a Court of law.

11. Power to make rules.--(1)
The Authority may, with the prior approval of Government and by notification in
the official Gazette make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.
(2) Without prejudice to the
foregoing powers, such rules may provide for:--
(a) procedure for registration,
licensing, renewal of registration of Blood Banks and fee to be paid for
registration, licensing and renewal of registration;.
(b) quality assurance in
maintenance of an effective anti-HIV Hepatitis, Malaria, Syphilis and other
viruses and infective agents screening;
(c) standard operating procedure
for evolving quality system of blood and blood products;
(d) safety measures to be adopted
in Blood Banks and laboratories; and
(e) screening and examination of
blood and blood products for detection of infectious agents.

SCHEDULE
(See Section 6(f))
BIO-SAFETY MEASURES
(a) Hands shall be washed before
and after each procedure, between each patient, before and after using gloves.
(b) No work shall be carried with
exposed skin, cuts and lesions inside the laboratory.
(c) Blood shall be drawn through
new disposable, sterilised syringes and needles.
(d) Blood shall not be pipette by
mouth.
(e) A freshly prepared solution of
10 % Sodium Hypochlorite shall always be available in the blood bank for
sterilisation of re-useable equipment i.e. pipettes, scissors, beakers, flasks
and other equipment.
(f) Needles and other sharp
instruments shall always be kept in rigid plastic, glass or metallic
containers.
(g) Needles shall be properly
capped.
(h) Decontaminate material shall
be autoclaved or burnt and buried at a scientific landfill site.
(i) Contaminated laboratory and
other clothing be autoclaved before sending them for washing.
(j) Work surfaces shall be
decontaminated with 10% Sodium Hypochlorite solution, bleach and soap at the
end of each day.
(k) All positive cases to be
notified to the Government on monthly basis on prescribed forms.
